title: Checkpoint: The First Artists
objective: After this level you can describe the earliest known art and the main ideas about why it was made.
summary: Radiocarbon dates charcoal back to about 50,000 years; uranium-series dates crusts over mineral paint, giving a minimum age. That's why records say 'at least'.

cards.headline: Chapter 1 finale: how do you date a painting nobody signed?
cards.body: Every date in this chapter came from a lab, not a label. Here's the whole chapter in order, then how those numbers were found, and why so many of them start with "at least".

events.label: An ochre crosshatch at Blombos Cave
A hand stencil on Muna island

cards.context: Radiocarbon dating measures carbon-14 in things that were once alive, like the burnt wood in charcoal, and works back to about 50,000 years. Many of Chauvet's black lines are charcoal, so labs can date the drawings themselves: most are about 35,500 years old. At Lascaux, charcoal from the cave gives about 17,000.

cards.headline: Why "at least"?
cards.body: Red ochre is iron oxide, a mineral, and many paintings have no organic material to date. So researchers date something else: thin mineral crusts that grew over the paint, using uranium, as at Leang Karampuang. The crust formed after the painting, so the paint must be older. That's a minimum age. The real one could be older, which is why records keep getting broken.

mascot.line: "At least 67,800 years" is science being honest. The hand might be older still.

cards.headline: Chapter 1 complete
learned: How art began with lines, hands and scenes on cave walls, long before anyone could write.
How labs put an age on cave paintings, and why so many records begin with 'at least'.
Why nobody knows for sure what cave art was for, and why hunting magic has a reindeer problem.
What counts as art, and why a sculpture of an idea can be art without looking like anything.

questions.prompt: Why is the Muna hand stencil dated "at least" 67,800 years old?

options.label: The lab lost part of the sample
options.rationale: Nothing went wrong; the method gives a minimum.

options.label: Radiocarbon can only estimate roughly
options.rationale: This date comes from uranium in mineral crusts.

options.label: The dated crust formed on top of the paint, after it
Scientists round every date down
options.rationale: It's not rounding; the paint is simply older than the crust.

questions.explanation: Uranium-series dating dates the crust over the paint. The paint came first, so it's at least that old.

questions.prompt: Radiocarbon needs something that was once alive. Which of these could it date directly?

options.label: A charcoal drawing of lions at Chauvet
A red ochre hand stencil
options.rationale: Red ochre is iron oxide, a mineral.

options.label: The limestone of the Willendorf figure
options.rationale: Limestone isn't charcoal or anything once alive.

options.label: A Stonehenge sarsen
options.rationale: A stone has no carbon from a living thing.

questions.explanation: Charcoal is burnt wood, once alive, so its carbon-14 can be measured.

questions.prompt: Chapter recap: which of these is the oldest?
questions.explanation: The Blombos drawing, about 73,000 years old, is the oldest known drawing.

questions.prompt: From Level 8: what did Göbekli Tepe show about hunter-gatherers?

options.label: They never stayed in one place
options.rationale: They came together to build something huge.

options.label: They could build a monument before farming
They copied Stonehenge
options.rationale: Göbekli Tepe is more than twice Stonehenge's age.

questions.explanation: Hunter-gatherers built its giant carved pillars about 11,500 years ago, before farming. Building together may even have led people to settle.

questions.prompt: From Level 4: which pair are complementary colors?

options.label: Red and orange
options.rationale: Neighbors on the wheel, not opposites.

options.label: Yellow and green
options.rationale: Green contains yellow, so they share a primary.

questions.explanation: Blue and orange sit opposite on the color wheel and share no primary.
